source_version.title: Rigorous derivation of the leapfrogging motion for planar Euler equations

findings.title: Incorrect density Hilbert conjugation changes the principal block and hides an all-parameter translation kernel
findings.claim: The conjugated order-epsilon^2 finite-rank operator supplies an invertible degenerate periodic block outside a discrete parameter set.
findings.check: For H e_j=i sign(j)e_j and B=f' composition(f), exact log-kernel conjugation has multiplier -2, not +1. The admissible b=t sin2theta, |t|<1/2, h=cos theta gives actual derivative -sin theta versus printed +sin theta/2. Correct Q=Qrot+Hhat0 annihilates h=cos(phi+theta), as does omega(partial_phi-partial_theta), for every permitted xi0.
findings.assumptions_verified: Real, smooth, zero theta mean; density change orientation preserving; fixed compact interval strictly inside(0,y0/sqrt2); common horizontal translation preserves conjugate and delayed geometry; no centroid gauge in H0 or Xs.
findings.counterevidence: Printed A0 determinant0.12126170473544845 and its characteristic polynomial are internally correct; initial-phase sign change is a constant diagonal conjugation. These do not identify the correct block.
findings.impact: Core leading inverse in Proposition5.1 and the subsequent approximate inverse is not established by the printed nonresonance calculation. Corrected monodromy has multiplier1 on the entire interval.

repair.required: New gauge/range/finite-dimensional solvability or another neutral-mode analysis, followed by inverse and iteration.

findings.deduplication: Hilbert coefficient and its monodromy consequence are one finding.

findings.title: Printed approximate solution retains a fourth-order residual required to be fifth order
findings.claim: The constructed r_epsilon satisfies G(epsilon r_epsilon)=O(epsilon^5).
findings.check: A1 omits -omega0 Theta_dot partial_theta g. At y0=1,xi0=1/2,O=[.45,.55],phi=0,theta=pi/4, a2=23/9,omega0 Theta_dot=16/3 and omitted coefficient736/27. Printed construction therefore gives epsilon^4*736/27+O(epsilon^5).
findings.assumptions_verified: All orbit/compact-interval conditions; g has only +/-2 modes, smooth zero mean; phase and q from specified point orbit.
findings.counterevidence: Existence of a corrected approximation is not refuted; even-mode inversion provides an explicit repair.
findings.impact: F(0) becomes O(epsilon^(2-mu)); multiplying by lambda^-1 gives epsilon^(-mu-delta), so the printed Nash–Moser initialization loses its smallness.

repair.statement: Replace r1 by r1+4 epsilon omega0 Theta_dot g, equivalently r_epsilon by r_epsilon+4epsilon^2 omega0 Theta_dot g. D0g=partial_theta g/4 cancels the missing coefficient; all sizes/even modes preserved.
repair.scope: Approximation step only; does not fix P1.

findings.title: High Sobolev input is not obtained by the printed interpolation and loss bookkeeping
findings.claim: Every choice satisfying(6.4) closes the inverse high-norm input and induction.
findings.check: (6.4) implies mu1>9a2, so exponent(mu1-a2)/2 is positive. Correct legal parameters(4,2,1/4,4,60,41,1/100,630,1400) give lower bound1315, L15,R155/2. The parameter-independent zero-mean sequence with frequencies floor(N^(1/4)) has low norms A*N^-4, high1400 norm A*N^(1369/4)<=A*N^630, but R norm A*N^(93/8) diverges.
findings.assumptions_verified: All strict source inequalities rechecked from actual source p55, including 4mu1/3. With N0 sufficiently large the frequencies are distinct and fit E_(n-1); weighted Lipschitz seminorm is zero. A fixed common prefactor enforces both low and high constants. The sequence tests only the low/high implication used, not nonlinear P2.
findings.counterevidence: b1 is freely selectable; strengthening it can make a smaller interpolation weight work. Correct derivative losses can be retained with residual decay.
findings.impact: The inverse cannot be invoked from the displayed induction hypotheses; limiting frequency also needs this high regularity.

repair.statement: Require b1>L+2(mu1+a2)(R-L)/a2, choose S sufficiently large and use theta=(R-L)/(b1-L). At b1=20000 kappa=8063/3997>2. Retain rho_(s+4tau+5), use high-norm smallness at low s and residual decay at high s. Missing2tau in(6.22) is absorbed by mu2>=4tau+3.

superseded_witness.invalid_reason: Source (6.4) has 4mu1/3, giving b1>1315; the previous lower bound895 omitted half of that term.

findings.title: Normalized stability lemma has wrong parameter scale and lacks the adapted state-difference bridge
findings.claim: Normalized c satisfies Delta c<=C(Delta c0+epsilon2 Delta rho) with proof c0=0.
findings.check: Take Omega1,c_-1=1/2,f0(rho)=rho constant,rho1=1/4,rho2=0,epsilon1=t,lambda=t^2,epsilon2=t^4,fixed largeN0. All absolute/high-norm conditions and t+N0^mu2*t^2 smallness hold. Iteration gives beta0,c=rho, so claimed uniform estimate would require1/4<=C*t^4/4.
findings.counterevidence: If c0 meant the first mean or lhs meant the full speed the test is avoided, but those readings change explicit definitions. Application has additional(4.6)–(4.7) structure; (4.26) is not disproved.
findings.impact: The general lemma invoked to justify the necessary limiting-frequency stability is invalid under its explicit normalization; primary[48] controls full speed under different norms/cutoffs and does not supply the adapted bridge.

repair.required: Distinguish normalized c/full C, identify base/first mean, add state-difference hypotheses and prove adapted epsilon/derivative estimates.

independent_acceptance_review.scope: Independent focused acceptance of all four numbered problems and the stated local corrections in arXiv:2311.15765v2, 5 December 2023, 81 pages. The admissibility of the old P3 witness was independently rejected and replaced with an actually checked witness. The source is not asserted equivalent to the publisher version. Root read the revised report and actually inspected all twelve current report pages; the native helper independently checked the specified source pages, assumptions, calculations, counterevidence and dependencies.

problems.independent_check: Under the source convention H e_j=i sign(j)e_j and the density conjugation B h=f' h composed with f, the first variation has coefficient -2 rather than the printed +1. With b=t sin(2 theta), h=cos(theta), the exact commutator gives -sin(theta), while the printed expression gives +sin(theta)/2. The corrected principal block Q=Q_rot+H_hat_0 annihilates the translation mode cos(phi+theta); the transport derivative partial_phi-partial_theta also annihilates it for every parameter xi.
problems.assumptions: The stated spaces impose zero spatial mean but no centroid gauge excluding this mode. The source Hilbert-transform sign, density factor and two-variable Fourier convention were checked.
problems.counterevidence: The determinant computation for the printed matrix is internally consistent; it does not verify the corrected operator. A kernel of the proposed inverse is not a nonexistence proof for the nonlinear Euler solutions.
problems.impact: The all-parameter neutral mode invalidates the presented inverse construction in the main existence chain.
problems.repair: A substantive treatment of neutral directions, range conditions and the approximate inverse is required; a complete repair was not established.

problems.independent_check: The approximate solution omits the contribution -omega_0 Theta_dot partial_theta g. The explicit permitted parameter y0=1, xi=1/2 has the stated harmonic coefficient23/9 and omega_0 Theta_dot=16/3; evaluation at theta=pi/4 yields the nonzero fourth-order residual736/27 times epsilon^4, incompatible with the required fifth order.
problems.assumptions: The harmonic is even and has zero spatial mean. The compact parameter range and the source's scaling of the normalized residual are retained.
problems.counterevidence: Adding the explicitly derived4 epsilon^2 omega_0 Theta_dot g term restores this local cancellation and preserves parity/mean. It does not remove P1's kernel.
problems.impact: The initial residual after the stated inverse loses the required smallness, so this is a core approximation input rather than a free-standing display error.
problems.repair: The local correction is verified; the full nonlinear construction remains conditional on the inverse and other inputs.

problems.independent_check: The actual source (6.4), p55, contains4 mu1/3. At the chosen parameters its lower bounds are1315 and149. The old b1=900 is inadmissible and is expressly superseded. Root saved and actually ran a new standard-library Fraction calculation: (s0,tau,mu,a2,a1,mu2,delta,mu1,b1)=(4,2,1/4,4,60,41,1/100,630,1400), L=15,R=155/2. All13 parameter/exponent/repair checks passed. For normalized real zero-mean Fourier increments u_k=A N_(k-1)^(-4) cos(m_k theta), with m_k=floor(N_(k-1)^(1/4)), frequency localization holds, the H^1400 exponent is1369/4<630, but the required H^R exponent is93/8>0. Orthogonality gives divergence after the harmless finite prefix is removed.
problems.assumptions: The sequence is parameter independent, with Lipschitz seminorm zero; the low/high norm bounds, frequency cutoff and all parameter inequalities actually used by the inference hold for sufficiently large N0 and fixed constants.
problems.counterevidence: This is a counterexample to the low/high interpolation inference. It is not asserted to satisfy the nonlinear residual condition P2 or to be an Euler solution.
problems.impact: The high norm needed before inversion and for the limiting frequency coefficient is not obtained by the printed argument.
problems.repair: A strengthened b1=20000 gives theta=25/7994 and kappa=8063/3997>2, restoring the stated narrow summation estimate conditionally. This does not repair the neutral-mode obstruction.

problems.independent_check: In Proposition A.9(4), c is the normalized correction and the proof initializes c0=0. Take Omega=1,c_-1=1/2,f0(rho)=rho for constant states rho1=1/4,rho2=0, epsilon1=t,lambda=t^2,epsilon2=t^4, with fixed sufficiently large N0. The absolute and smallness assumptions hold as t tends to0. The homological equation has no nonconstant modes; its recurrence gives beta=0 and c=rho exactly. The claimed estimate would require1/4<=C t^4/4, impossible uniformly.
problems.assumptions: No spatial-mean restriction on these constant states is present in the general appendix proposition. Absolute state bounds are distinguished from the missing difference hypotheses.
problems.counterevidence: Interpreting c0 as the mean of f0 or replacing c with the full transport speed changes the actual defined statement. The cited Hmidi-Roulley result controls the full coefficient with different hypotheses. The particular application (4.26) has extra structure and is not disproved by this example.
problems.impact: The false general normalized estimate is the stated stability bridge used in the Cantor-parameter argument.
problems.repair: Restate and prove an adapted full-coefficient difference estimate with the actual losses and parameters. No complete repaired bridge was certified.

local_checks.check: The reduced Hamiltonian, compact noncolliding periodic orbit, corrected elliptic parameter and positive derivative identities support the period/twist input. Coordinate and time rescaling distinguish neutral/transverse stability from existence. Historical finite numerical checks are corroborative, not interval certificates.

The final cross-interaction half coefficient is correct despite an intermediate missing half; the delayed kernel label and extra epsilon factor are local corrections. Conditional on a small valid solution, zero mean fixes circulation and the compact-range separation gives disjoint patches.

The retained exact quadrupole Bezout identity supports non-rigidity throughout the admissible interval, conditional on the construction. The high-mode lambda^-1 inverse and Fourier-support cancellation do not resolve the translation mode.

Piecewise linear interpolation of the real parameter preserves the stated Hilbert/Lipschitz bounds. The corrected finite-difference estimate retains lambda^-1, yet epsilon^3/lambda tends to0 and suffices for the stated conditional resonance-measure order. One optimized derivative economy remains unverified and is not counted as a further error.
